source.title: Is deeper better? It depends on locality of relevant features

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study experimentally tests how depth, width, and learning rate relate to test error in overparameterized networks, but on synthetic local/global labels and an Ising task rather than the settings named in the versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports comparisons of finite networks and NTKs as study results; cited findings from prior work are not extracted. Figure-only numerical values are not reconstructed.
record.test_reason: The study tests V2 in new synthetic classification settings: networks are trained to zero training error, and wider networks achieve lower test error within this interpolating regime. A sweep across the interpolation threshold is unnecessary to test this post-interpolation width effect. Most extracted rows instead concern depth, NTKs, or input stability.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct, with the qualification that the deeper-network advantage concerns nonlinear local labels with k ≥ 2; for 1-local labels, shallower networks perform better. Chaotic signal propagation is proposed as a possible mechanism, not established causally. The authors also emphasize that optimized finite networks can depart from NTK predictions and demonstrate a shallow-network advantage on the Ising task.
record.recipe_differences: Studies synthetic Gaussian-input local/global-label tasks and an Ising spin-configuration task using fully connected networks; it does not reproduce the listed studies' settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth effects differ by label locality; width changes test error and variance in some settings; learning-rate sensitivity differs by task and depth; loss choice changes quantitative generalization and width dependence.

fits_no_version.finding: For nonlinear local labels, deeper networks generally perform better; for global labels, shallower networks perform better. Small training sets can prevent the narrow deep network from generalizing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization effect of depth depends on the locality and complexity of relevant features.

fits_no_version.finding: NTKs fail on higher-order local labels despite successful finite-network classification; on 3-global labels, depth-7 NTK succeeds while depth-1 NTK fails.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NTK predictions need not capture finite-network generalization or its depth dependence under optimized learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: Learning-rate choice changes test error and can reverse shallow-versus-deep rankings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth comparisons depend on whether training operates in a lazy or feature-learning regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Deep networks trained on random labels show lower stability under local input perturbations than shallow networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth affects the locality of learned prediction functions even on structureless labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Shallow networks outperform deep networks on Ising temperature classification at larger training-set sizes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shallower networks can generalize better on classification tasks governed by global thermodynamic features.

record.problems: The principal tasks use artificial Gaussian inputs and constructed local/global labels; the authors note that application to a wider class of real datasets remains future work. Many results are presented in figures without exact numerical values in the text. Learning rates are optimized by validation, so the reported depth comparisons depend on that procedure.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-version rows were omitted; the measured findings do not match the specific settings or measures in V1–V8. Exact plotted values were not reconstructed.

untested.parts: No matched comparison of natural-label generalization, random-label fitting, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.

The original image benchmarks, a width sweep locating the zero-training-error threshold, and behavior below that threshold are untested. Training stops at zero classification error rather than demonstrating loss convergence.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison or learned-local-connectivity intervention.
Batch size is fixed at 50; no batch-size or fixed-epoch-budget comparison.
No magnitude-aware weight perturbations, generalization-gap ranking, or comparison with norm and margin measures.
No removal of memorized examples and retraining comparison.

missing.what: Within-depth width comparisons for 1-local and 1-global labels: Section 3.1 explicitly reports decreasing test error with width. Figure 1 compares H = 500 versus 2000 at L = 1 and H = 100 versus 500 at L = 7, with training to zero error.
The explicit result that widening higher-order local-label networks reduces both test error and variability from initialization and training is absent from the recorded row values.

Loss-dependent width comparisons: under mean-square loss, the depth-7, width-100 network fails to generalize well through N = 30000 on 3-local labels, whereas width 500 generalizes. This width dependence is stronger than under cross-entropy.
missing.locator: Supplementary Material B; Figure S1(b), compared with Figure 2(b)

record.verdict_notes: Different datasets do not by themselves make a width-generalization result irrelevant to V2. The record overlooks direct post-interpolation width evidence. No listed original source is this study. States marked cannot_determine on unlinked rows indicate that their measures cannot establish a listed version, not that their reported depth or stability findings are unreadable.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting natural labels with fitting random labels or report natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Does not test one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10, or sweep width past the zero-training-error threshold in those settings.
Uses fully connected networks; does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on image datasets or test local connectivity.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
Fixes mini-batch size at 50; does not vary batch size.
Measures local stability, not magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized examples or measure the resulting test-accuracy change.

relationships.condition: Synthetic Gaussian-input classification with validation-selected learning rates and training to zero classification error.
relationships.reason: R4 reports improved generalization from widening depth-7 networks on 3-global labels; additional text-only results in Sections 3.1–3.2 report lower test error with width for 1-local, 1-global, and higher-order local labels. Those additional comparisons need rows.
relationships.display_finding: The reported test-error reductions from widening networks trained to zero classification error remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
